reference_preprocessing: The LoC master is a STEREOGRAPH: two frames on a printed mount with publisher text down both margins and a caption block. Fed whole it risked importing the card format or its lettering into a plate whose NEVER list forbids text. Cropped to ONE clean frame and resized to 1920x1080 before use; all refs pre-sized so the first sets the aspect ratio.
method_note: Gated against the NEVER list AND an exploratory pass ('is anything in frame that is not specified'), because a NEVER list is confirmatory by construction and cannot catch what nobody listed. The exploratory pass is what caught the caption text on the rejected candidates.
subject: ENVIRONMENT PLATE — the 1870s excavation at the Temple of Zeus, empty.
rejected: none — cand/env_2.png also passes every NEVER and is a valid alternate with a denser drum field
rejected_why: env_1 selected because its TWO parallel drum rows flanking a central trench read as the temple's two LONG SIDES, the architectural claim in the brief; env_2's drums mass centre-left instead.
never_checked: no standing colonnade and no upright columns — every drum lies fallen
no mountain range, snow or sea
no modern paths, ropes, signs or barriers
no visitors or any human figure
asserts: Kronos hill present, rounded, densely wooded, filling the upper third
fallen Doric drums in long lines along the temple's long sides
raw earth trench walls with tool marks, gravel spoil heaps, bare dirt — a working dig
hard high sun, strong shadows, dust
exploratory_note: A pale vertical form in the midground was checked at 3x in case it was an upright column — it is a squat rectangular block on the trench lip with others beside it. Not a column. Checked because it is the NEVER that matters most for 1875.
